themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 118 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 27.4 weekly average—a 331% increase (z-score: 8.61)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in road quality across Woodhaven/Richmond Hill that demands urgent investigation into what triggered this rapid degradation.
evidence: 118 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 27.4 weekly baseline (331% increase, z-score 8.61)
Street Sign - Damaged spike of 300% (7 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.8 baseline) suggests infrastructure-wide stress
Sewer complaints up 209% last week (22 vs. 7.1 baseline), indicating possible subsurface infrastructure failure affecting streets
reporting_angles: Did recent weather events, heavy truck traffic, or deferred maintenance trigger the street deterioration spike?
Which specific streets or corridors are experiencing the worst conditions? Conduct ground-truth reporting in highest-complaint areas.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 10 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.9 weekly—a 1043% spike (z-score: 11.69)—indicating a sudden surge in Uber/Lyft activity or aggressive driving behavior concentrated in this single week.
evidence: 10 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (1043% increase, z-score 11.69)
Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints also spiked to 21 THIS WEEK (217% increase), consistent with increased vehicle activity
Street condition spike this week may be exacerbated by heavy for-hire vehicle congestion and usage patterns
reporting_angles: Why did for-hire vehicle complaints spike so suddenly this week? Interview residents in complaint hotspots about gridlock, blocking, and unsafe driving.
Are ride-share companies concentrating pickups/dropoffs in specific areas? Check if new restaurants, bars, or transit hubs are driving demand.

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Failure
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints exploded 3100% two weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score: 11.72)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset—suggesting a significant sanitation service disruption or enforcement breakdown that may persist.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% increase, z-score 11.72—highest anomaly in dataset)
Unsanitary condition complaints (249 total over 90 days) suggest chronic sanitation stress independent of street sweeping
Rodent complaints up 433% THIS WEEK (6 vs. 1.1 baseline), potentially linked to inadequate street cleaning creating food sources
reporting_angles: Did Sanitation Department reduce street sweeping frequency or routes in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill two weeks ago?
Interview residents and local businesses: Has visible trash accumulation worsened? Are rodent complaints correlated with dirty streets?

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Outages
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints spiked to 165 two weeks ago from a 30.0 weekly baseline—a 450% increase (z-score: 4.97)—creating potential safety and congestion hazards if signals remain malfunctioning.
evidence: 165 traffic signal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 30.0 weekly baseline (450% increase, z-score 4.97)
Street condition spike THIS WEEK combined with signal failures suggests infrastructure-wide emergency
Illegal parking (4,782 complaints over 90 days) and blocked driveway complaints (2,389) may worsen if signals fail and traffic management breaks down
reporting_angles: How many traffic signals are currently inoperable or malfunctioning in CD 409? Has DOT issued repair schedules?
Have residents reported accidents or near-misses at signal-problem intersections? Safety audit needed.

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a 1.1 weekly baseline—a 433% increase (z-score: 4.63)—coinciding with the street sweeping failure and unsanitary conditions, suggesting an emerging pest crisis if cleaning and waste management don't improve.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (433% increase, z-score 4.63)
Street sweeping collapse 2 weeks ago (3100% spike) likely eliminated street-level sanitation, creating breeding environment
Unsanitary condition complaints persist as chronic baseline (249 over 90 days), now compounded by acute pest surge
reporting_angles: Interview residents in areas with spike in complaints: Where are rats being spotted? Are they in homes, streets, or commercial areas?
Is lack of street cleaning correlating with rodent sightings? Investigate Sanitation Department response and timeline for pest control.
